label: Pope visit
description: Visit of Pope Leo XIV to Paris on 25-26 Sept; Vélib' Métropole set up two temporary giant stations (400 docks each, 800 in total) at La Madeleine and near Pont des Invalides for the Mass on Saturday 26 Sept (Concorde / lower Champs-Élysées). Compare with the event stations (capacity 100 or more) in the data. The sector closures (Champs-Élysées from 17 Sept) come from the operator blog, which we could not reach on 23 Nov: not confirmed.

label: Strike day 29 Sept
description: National public-sector strike (civil servants, hospitals, schools, firefighters) against the pay freeze; more than 170 rallies in France and a march in Paris in the afternoon; some RER and Transilien lines disrupted. Previous source URL pointed to an article about 6 Oct and was replaced.

label: High-school blockades 2 Oct
description: High-school blockade day: about 400 lycées closed in France as a safety measure, Paris lycées blocked (e.g. Voltaire, Hélène-Boucher); no large Paris march confirmed for this day. The previous source URL (France 3) described the 2 October 2025 march, not 2026, and was replaced.

label: High-school and student march
description: National high-school and student march, Place de la République to Place de la Nation via Boulevard Voltaire, from 14:00. Interior Ministry count: about 266,000 people in France, 56,000 in Paris; tear gas at Place de la Nation at the end.

label: Student rally Bastille
description: High-school and student rally at Place de la Bastille, 15:00 (and an early-childhood strike gathering in the 14th at 10:00).

label: Strike 13 Oct
description: Strike of students and education staff: main march from Place d'Italie to Les Invalides from 14:00; a second student march from Hôtel de Ville to Matignon; several metro stations closed from 09:00.

label: 17 Oct riots
description: National march against the cost of living; riots and looting in Paris. Smovengo (operator) reports heavy damage at 6 stations (2 very heavily damaged) and at more than 30 docks, and nearly 300 Vélib' bikes damaged or stolen, mainly around République, Gare du Nord, Saint-Lazare, Bastille, Voltaire and Châtelet (AFP). The bike counts are context only: the feed cannot show them.

label: Rally 22 Oct (march banned)
description: Students' march banned by the prefecture on 21 Oct; the administrative court lifted the ban on 22 Oct but a new order imposed a static rally outside Pitié-Salpêtrière (13th) from 14:00; the article mentions several previous nights of curfew without dates. Note: our out-of-service peak (22 Oct 23:00 UTC = 23 Oct 01:00 Paris) matches the start of the E09 closure, not this rally.

label: 110 stations closed (24 Oct)
description: At the prefecture's request, 110 Vélib' stations closed in the security perimeters from Friday 23 Oct for the 24 Oct demonstration (article updated 23 Oct 18:30). The 31 Oct article (E10) says the same stations were closed for 24 Oct; station list in closed_stations_E09.csv (copied from the E10 article). Reopening time for this weekend not confirmed (operator blog unreachable).

label: 110 stations closed (31 Oct)
description: Second, separate closure: 110 stations neutralised from Friday 30 Oct for the 31 Oct demonstration (protest against the cost of living), arrondissements 1 to 20, reopening gradually overnight Sunday 1 Nov into Monday 2 Nov (article updated 30 Oct 17:40). Same stations as for 24 Oct per the article; list in closed_stations_E10.csv.

label: National mobilisation 14 Nov
description: National mobilisation: 106,000 people in France (137 actions), 24,000 in Paris according to the Interior Ministry; the Paris march took place in good conditions.

label: National action day 5 Nov
description: High-school mobilisation and national action day: 575,000 people in France, 65,000 in Paris according to the Interior Ministry. Added on 23 Nov (was missing from the list).

label: Mobilisation 7 Nov
description: Saturday mobilisation against the cost of living: 146,000 people in France, 46,000 in Paris according to the Interior Ministry; incidents in large cities. Added on 23 Nov (was missing from the list).
